**Rules:** Throw rings onto bottles (make three Dexterity checks, no modifier)


** 3 tosses, 3 times a day**

**Limit one of each prize per player.**

**If lost, (18 or lower for all three rings) **
A cacophony of little voices let out sighs and sounds of consolation.

**DC 19**
**1 ring**- fingerless leather gloves that automatically change style to fit the latest fashion trends
If won, post: squeals and clapping abound, the small pom-pom like creatures hand you a pair of fingerless gloves.

**2 rings**- Rope of mending A rope of mending looked like a regular rope made of hemp. It was sold in coils of 50 feet (15 meters). If the rope was cut into smaller lengths, it could be mended by uttering a special command word. The shortened lengths had to be in contact with one another and not in use for the mending to be successful.
If won, post: Shrill sounds escape the furry booth attendants, they seem excited for you. Together, they manage to get a rope down from the top of the booth and lay it on the counter. 

**3 rings**-Whisper Powder-Wondrous item (consumable) A shimmering fae powder that when sprinkled on a creature affects only them with the silence spell. While affected this way you have advantage on stealth checks to not be heard. The effect lasts for 10 minutes.
If won, post: Silence befalls the booth as soon as the third ring settles on the bottle. All of the furry creatures stop and stare at you. An explosion of celebration begins; some are high fiving each other, others are squealing in delight as they hang from the rafters, one looks you in the eye and slides you a small pouch at the end of a corded necklace. You don't know what it is for, but clearly you have earned it.

You walk up to this dark and luxuriously decorated booth to see three cups on a table. Behind the counter is an Owlfolk teen who seems disinterested in you and the surroundings of Coney Island. They stick out their hand for tickets. “Three tries.” they state.
Once you give them the tickets they sigh, show you a ball under one of the three cups, and begins to absentmindedly moving the cups around. Faster and faster, until the cups are almost blurring together. Then they stop. “Well? Where’s the ball?”

**Rules:  Which cup is the ball under? (make a wisdom check, no modifier)

3 tries per day.

Limit one of each prize per player.**

**If lost (18 or lower on all 3)**
The teen looks at you with a small smirk “Bummer.”

**DC 19**
**1 correct**- Elder’s Necklace - 3 times a day, you can make your voice sound like that of a wise elders’. This only works if you are giving unsolicited advice 
If won, post: The teen grabs a necklace from behind the counter and hands it to you. “Here.”

**2 correct**- Sending stone. Just the one. Someone (a raving lunatic)  has the other.
If won, post: They hand you a single sending stone and say “Not bad.”

**3 correct-** Eyes of the Eagle wood rimmed glasses
If won, post: They reach under the counter and pull out a pair of wood-rimmed circular glasses. “Nice.” They say actually seeming a little impressed.

As you walk up to this booth you see a rather pale looking dwarf sitting behind the counter. Tankards of various sizes hang from the rafters. The Dwarf sees you approach and pours a bubbly drink into a mug and nudges it your way with a grunt. “Drink”. It smells incredibly inviting but something in the back of your brain screams “CAREFUL!”

**Rules: Drink the fluid. Don't throw up. (Make a constitution check, no modifier)

3 tries per day.

Limit one of each prize per player.**

**If 14 or lower:** Your stomach churns, something about that drink doesn’t sit right with you. Seeing the look in your eye, Donnie pushes a bucket your way. You are unable to hold the drink down any longer. You also have disadvantage on constitution checks for the next 30 minutes.

**DC 15-** (Load stone tankard weighs 1 pound empty, 50 pounds full)
If won, post: Donnie tips his chair back, grabs a tankard from a barrel behind him, and tosses it your way. 

**DC19-** Fey-aged fizz (the drink you are drinking. When drunk, roll of fey wild magic table)
If won, post: Donnie grunts and slides you a bottle from under the counter. It is labeled ‘Fey-aged Fizz’ upon further inspection it is the drink he was pouring you. 

**DC 23- **Tankard of Sobriety (can't get drunk if drinking from this mug)
If won, post: Donnie grunts and slides you a shiney tankard. It may be in your head but you swear you saw the side of his mouth curl up for a half a second.

This booth is build around a giant tree who is also its attendant. A few prizes line the walls, but otherwise there seems to be no obvious game. “Welcome…...fellow mage…...how well do you know……..your spells……... and all that they……... require?” He speaks slowly, painfully so.

**Rules: Guess the spell based on the components (make an intelligence check, no modifier)

3 tries per day.

Limit one of each prize per player.**

**If lost (roll 18 or lower on all 3) post:**
“Deepest…….of…….condolences………….. It seems……… as if…...you are……..in need……. of further………. studying……. Of the arcane………...arts.”

**DC 19**
**1 correct** -A monocle that prohibits you from speaking in words that are less than 4 syllables.
If won, post: “It looks……….as if……………you know……..a few things………….about…...magic! Here…….. Is a……………..monocle. It…….. makes you……...sound……..smarter……...than you are.”

**2 correct-** Tricorn hat of thought . This hat allows you to remember historical events with near perfect accuracy. (Adv on history checks)
If won post: “Well……………...well……….well. Quite……...impressive!” He hands you a tricorn hat. “This……..hat……...helps one…….remember……….better.”

**3 correct**- Poor Richard's Almanac (attuned). A guide book and record of the past that allows you to see trajectories easier and your spell casting range for ranged spells increases by 10ft
If won, post: “Astonishing!........you seem……...to really……...know a lot……….about the……… arcane.” He hands you a book entitled ‘Poor Richards’ Almanac’ and continues “Perhaps……… you will……..find this……..as interesting……..as I……….did.”

This booth is a stage full of lights with three judges (a Puffkin, a Tortle, and a Seelie Fey) in front of the stage on their own platform, looking bored.

**Step right up and take your place amongst Empire City’s best entertainers! (Make a Charisma check, no modifier) Also RP your performance.

1 try per day. Limit one of each prize per player.**


**If 14 or lower:** The judges lean in to deliberate. After a few moments they turn back to you. “I’m sorry,” says Poppy “Unfortunately we have decided that your performance today wasn’t enough for a prize. Come back another day and try again! I’m sure you’ll get there!” 

**DC 15**- Fannypack of Glamour
If won, post: The three judges all lean in to deliberate amongst themselves. Poppy walks up to you and hands you a shiny small bag with a very short strap. It has rainbow sequins all over it. “Congrats you won the fanny pack of glamour! You wear it around your hips!” This bag holds “things” and its really pretty. 

**DC 19**- Wand of Smiles
If won, post: Poppy hands you a wooden wand with what looks like teeth inlayed into it. “Wonderful work up there! Here’s a wand that’ll make anyone you point it at smile for a whole minute! But you can only use it thrice daily. Enjoy!” 

**DC 23**- Instrument of Illusions
If won, post: Poppy steps up to you and points to three instruments on the side of the stage. “Pick one!” (Choose whatever instrument you want it to be) “You sure deserve it for that performance!”  (While you are playing this musical instrument, you can create harmless, illusory visual effects within a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on the instrument. If you are a bard, the radius increases to 15 feet. Sample visual effects include luminous musical notes, a spectral dancer, butterflies, and gently falling snow.)

This hotel is known for its opulence, unpredictability, and secrecy. Boasting stunning views of the ocean and grown entirely of huge trees intertwining, it is no wonder this hotel has become a sought after vacation spot. Hiring only the best entertainers with the most fabulous costumes, and the most over the top talents Boompaleis provides an experience you won't soon forget. What happens in Boompaleis stays in Boompaleis. 

3000g per room per night. Rooms fit up to 4 people.  Trust us, its worth it, everone says so, but no one you talk to can give any specifics.

?message
`?message (timestamp) (channel) (message text)`

Allows adding a scheduled bot message through a command in Discord instead of files on Dropbox.
The timestamp must be either `HH:MM` for messages to be sent once daily,
or `YY-MM-DD HH:MM` for messages to be sent only once. 24-hour clock, server time.
The channel must be either the channel name raw, or the #-link to it.

Everything from the new line after that onwards is treated as the message content.
In the message you can put regular Discord mentions, both to specific people and roles, or everyone,
as well as #-links to channels.
Alternatively you can use the square brackets notation made for the bot for adding messages directly in files:
- #[channel-name-or-id] will convert into a link to a channel specified by the name or id in square brackets.
- @[something] will try to parse the contents either to a role (exact match), or a specific person.
For getting specific people, you have options:
- @[user-id-number] will directly match the person
- @[current-name-in-server] will match if they have been active in the last 24h (same functionality as ?where)
- @[name-or-start-of-one] will try to find a member whose username or server nickname matches the input.
For example, @[ver] would match Versil if there were no other possibilities.
Usage of square brackets mention substitutes is msotly there so you don't have to ping a person when setting this.

The bot will list what it read from your message, including all the mentions it found and parsed.
That way you can verify if everything's as you expected, and you then have to confirm it.
Anything other than "no", "n", "0" or "nah" as your response will be treated as confirmation.

This method also has a variant, `?message interactive` (or `?message assist` or `?message i`).
That one will guide you through the process step by step without having to remember what goes where.
